3 Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel; (1 Peter 3:3 KJV)

Some religious people are using verses like this to say that women have to dress in a certain way, but that is not what Peter was saying. He was saying that we should not let the clothes we wear, and our jewelry, and our hair fixing, be the important thing in our lives, but that we need to have our inner person right with God, and not concentrate on the outward appearance. Why some religious people try to always relate to the carnal outward man, instead of realizing what the Word is teaching, I don’t understand. In context, all Peter is saying is that our outward appearance is not what is important, but what is in our hearts is what matters to God. As God’s Word tells us that God looks on the heart, whereas man looks on the outward appearance (1 Samuel 16:7).

This type of teaching that religious preachers are doing, just illustrates that they are teaching the Law, and not the Grace of Jesus, and are making the Cross of Jesus of no effect in their lives. You can not live by the law of doing, and be saved by the law of Grace, as Jesus said you don’t put new wine in old wineskins, or they will break (Matthew 9:17). You can not mix the Old Testament Law with the New Testament Grace, as the two will not mix (Romans 11:6). If you are doing things to be right with God, you are under the law, but if you are putting all your trust in Jesus by faith, you are under the Grace of God, and He does not look at what you do (Hebrews 10:17). Just trust our Savior Jesus, and rest in His Grace. We are living in a period called the Lord’s Rest, and we are supposed to quit trying to earn God’s blessings, and just rest in His Grace brought to us through Jesus. Praise God for His Grace in saving us in such a wonderful manner, even though we don’t deserve it. Thank you Jesus for our salvation.
